chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskān, from al-Ḥalabī, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh (peace be upon him) said: My father used to give legal rulings, and we used to give legal rulings while we were fearful regarding the hunting of hawks and falcons. But now, we are not fearful.
And we do not permit their hunting unless their slaughter (death by bleeding) is achieved.
And indeed it is in the Book of Allah, Exalted and Glorified, that Allah, Exalted and Glorified, said: 'What you have taught of the hunting beasts, making them train.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on eating hawks and falcons caught for hunting?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling on consuming birds of prey, noting a shift from earlier caution to a permissive stance provided the animal is slaughtered (dhakat), drawing an analogy to the Quranic verse on hunting beasts. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of extending the permissibility of land animals to birds of prey when the method of slaughter is applied, distinguishing it from the general prohibition of non-slaughtered game. The reference to 'beasts' (al-jawāriḥ) serves as the textual basis for including these birds within the category of permissible game under specific conditions.
